# Start here

This notebook continues from the **existing monthly NetCDF products** of
`reynolds_decomposition.qmd`. It does not download ERA5, filter winds, or rerun
the Reynolds decomposition. It contains the implemented scope of the original
framework: monthly preparation and diagnostics, energy characterization,
annual and seasonal Pan-Arctic trends, and spatial trend maps for five metrics.
The former roadmap's regional and attribution studies were not implemented;
this revision does not present them as completed analyses.

Read and run the notebook from top to bottom. Each stage explains its purpose,
the objects it creates, and how to interpret the outputs. Start in
`setup-environment`: check **DATA_DIRECTORY** and **LEGACY_DATA_DIR**. All
corrected tables, figures and caches are written into separate directories.
The input NetCDF files and old analysis outputs are read only.

| Stage | What happens | Main object/output |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Setup and shared functions | Paths, controls, date and statistical helpers | One configuration chunk |
| 1. Read and verify data | Decode actual months, align grids, area-weight monthly fields | `storm_df`, input audit |
| 2. Understand variability | Summary statistics, ACF/PACF, STL, climatologies | Diagnostic CSVs and figures |
| 3. Describe energy | Monthly Reynolds energy partition and EKE comparison | Original Phase 2 figures |
| 4. Estimate domain trends | Zhang slopes/tests and matching residual bootstrap intervals | 8 annual and 32 seasonal rows |
| 5. Examine spatial trends | Check/reuse cached local tests; calculate BH; draw maps | 25-field local/BH summary |
| 6. Review outputs | Session details and a file inventory | Submission review checklist |

**What has changed scientifically?** The reported Zhang slope is retained, but
its bootstrap now repeats the same estimator. Blocks are selected from fitted
residuals. The confidence intervals must therefore be regenerated. BH results
are calculated from the actual local p-values rather than assumed to be zero.
Rejection fractions are descriptive and are not labelled field-significance
tests. Complete annual/seasonal trend periods remain 1958–2025.

**A boundary correction:** `storm_df` includes December 1957 for DJF 1958.
Calendar-month diagnostics and annual climatologies use January 1958–December
2025 (816 months). Seasonal climatologies use 68 complete seasons, so DJF uses
December 1957–February 2025 and excludes December 2025. Small changes from old
summary values that mixed these windows are expected.

**Execution status:** all code chunks were parsed by R. The date, DJF and BH
self-checks were executed. A synthetic-series test using `zyp`, `boot` and
`blocklength` checked preservation of the original point estimate/p-value,
finite bootstrap output and reproducibility with a fixed seed. These checks
used a lightweight R runtime, not the actual ERA5 data. NetCDF processing,
full spatial execution and figure layout must still be verified on the local
R installation; no full ERA5 run is claimed here.

# 0. Configure the analysis

## 0.1 Environment and settings

Keep all routine edits here. Packages are checked, not installed automatically.
If packages are missing, run the printed installation command in the R console
and rerun this chunk. Python/reticulate is unnecessary for this downstream R
analysis; the original Python preprocessing environment is unaffected.

`ALLOW_SPATIAL_RECOMPUTE = FALSE` prevents an unexpected full spatial rerun.
The old cache is first checked against actual months, coordinates, and 24
sampled grid points in every variable/period. Passing these checks supports
reuse but cannot reconstruct missing historical provenance. If a cache is
incompatible, the notebook stops with a specific message; it does not guess.

## 0.2 Shared functions: read once, reuse throughout

A **function** gives a name to a repeated task. Defining it does not run the
analysis: the later chunks supply its input and use its result. The time helper
reads CF units from each file. It truncates sub-millisecond precision in the
origin for month identification, avoiding rounding an end-of-month timestamp
into the next month. Dates must match every expected month, in order.

`read_cube()` uses dimension **names**, rather than guessing from array sizes.
`prepare_variable()` reads a few months at a time and uses cosine-latitude
weights. Missing Arctic cells stop the run so that the geographical footprint
does not silently change. The old NetCDF name `eke_mean` is accepted as an
in-memory alias for `eke_synoptic_mean`.

```{r data-helpers}
# Each helper has one job. Functions are defined here, then called below.
# They do not open or alter the preprocessing wind files.

assert_that <- function(ok, message) {
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) stop(message, call. = FALSE)
}

# A small fingerprint records settings/data in caches without hashing a huge
# NetCDF file on every run. File identity below uses path, size and mtime.
object_hash <- function(x) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
  on.exit(unlink(f), add = TRUE)
  saveRDS(x, f, version = 2)
  unname(tools::md5sum(f))
}
file_identity <- function(path) {
  info <- file.info(path)
  assert_that(!is.na(info$size), paste("Missing input:", path))
  list(path = normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE),
       bytes = unname(info$size), modified = as.numeric(info$mtime))
}
write_rds <- function(x, path) {
  # Write to a temporary sibling first. A failed calculation never writes a
  # partially built object into its final cache. Only corrected caches change.
  tmp <- tempfile(tmpdir = dirname(path), fileext = ".rds")
  on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
  saveRDS(x, tmp)
  assert_that(file.copy(tmp, path, overwrite = TRUE), paste("Cannot save:", path))
}

# ---- CF time: decode the FILE coordinate; never invent an 817-row sequence ----
decode_months <- function(raw, units, calendar = "standard") {
  assert_that(calendar %in% c("standard", "gregorian", "proleptic_gregorian"),
              paste("Unsupported calendar:", calendar))
  match <- regexec("^(days|hours|minutes|seconds|milliseconds|microseconds) since (.+)$",
                   trimws(units))
  parts <- regmatches(trimws(units), match)[[1]]
  assert_that(length(parts) == 3L, paste("Unsupported time units:", units))
  factor_sec <- c(days = 86400, hours = 3600, minutes = 60, seconds = 1,
                  milliseconds = 0.001, microseconds = 0.000001)[parts[2]]
  origin <- sub("T", " ", parts[3], fixed = TRUE)
  origin <- sub("( UTC|Z| ?\\+00:00)$", "", origin)
  if (grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$", origin)) origin <- paste(origin, "00:00:00")
  assert_that(grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2} \\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}(\\.\\d+)?$", origin),
              paste("Unrecognized time origin:", origin))
  # pandas end_time is 23:59:59.999999999. POSIXct cannot keep nanoseconds.
  # Truncate the origin's fraction to milliseconds, rather than rounding it
  # into the next month. This changes <1 ms and is used ONLY to identify months.
  origin <- sub("(\\.\\d{3})\\d+", "\\1", origin)
  t0 <- as.POSIXct(origin, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", tz = "UTC")
  assert_that(!is.na(t0) && all(is.finite(raw)), "Invalid time coordinate.")
  stamps <- t0 + as.numeric(raw) * factor_sec
  as.Date(format(stamps, "%Y-%m-01", tz = "UTC"))
}

read_metadata <- function(path) {
  nc <- ncdf4::nc_open(path)
  on.exit(ncdf4::nc_close(nc), add = TRUE)
  raw <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "time")
  units <- ncdf4::ncatt_get(nc, "time", "units")$value
  ca <- ncdf4::ncatt_get(nc, "time", "calendar")
  calendar <- if (isTRUE(ca$hasatt)) ca$value else "standard"
  dates <- decode_months(raw, units, calendar)
  expected <- seq(MONTH_START, MONTH_END, by = "month")
  assert_that(identical(as.character(dates), as.character(expected)),
    paste(basename(path), "must contain each month, in order, from",
          MONTH_START, "to", MONTH_END, "with no duplicates or gaps."))
  lat <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "latitude")
  lon <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "longitude")
  assert_that(length(lat) > 1L && length(lon) > 1L &&
                all(is.finite(lat)) && all(is.finite(lon)), "Invalid spatial coordinates.")
  assert_that(all(diff(lat) > 0) || all(diff(lat) < 0), "Latitude must be monotonic.")
  assert_that(all(diff(lon) > 0), "Longitude must be increasing.")
  assert_that(max(abs(diff(lon) - median(diff(lon)))) < 1e-5 &&
                abs(length(lon) * median(diff(lon)) - 360) < 1e-3,
              "Expected a complete, regular longitude grid without a duplicate endpoint.")
  assert_that(max(abs(abs(diff(lat)) - median(abs(diff(lat))))) < 1e-5,
              "Cosine weighting here requires regular latitude spacing.")
  list(path = path, raw_time = raw, time_units = units, dates = dates,
       calendar = calendar, lat = lat, lon = lon, variables = names(nc$var),
       identity = file_identity(path))
}

resolve_variable <- function(nc, variable) {
  # Accept the old name in memory: no rename/overwrite of the source NetCDF.
  actual <- if (variable == "eke_synoptic_mean" &&
                 !variable %in% names(nc$var) && "eke_mean" %in% names(nc$var))
    "eke_mean" else variable
  assert_that(actual %in% names(nc$var), paste("Missing variable:", variable))
  actual
}
read_cube <- function(nc, variable, time_start = 1L, time_count = -1L) {
  actual <- resolve_variable(nc, variable)
  dn <- vapply(nc$var[[actual]]$dim, function(d) d$name, character(1))
  target <- c("time", "latitude", "longitude")
  assert_that(length(dn) == 3L && setequal(dn, target),
              paste(actual, "must have time, latitude and longitude dimensions."))
  start <- rep(1L, 3); count <- rep(-1L, 3)
  start[match("time", dn)] <- time_start
  count[match("time", dn)] <- time_count
  arr <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, actual, start = start, count = count,
                          collapse_degen = FALSE)
  aperm(arr, match(target, dn)) # now ALWAYS [time, latitude, longitude]
}

month_index <- function(dates) {
  y <- as.integer(format(dates, "%Y")); m <- as.integer(format(dates, "%m"))
  tibble(date = dates, year = y, month = m,
    season = c("DJF", "DJF", "MAM", "MAM", "MAM", "JJA",
               "JJA", "JJA", "SON", "SON", "SON", "DJF")[m],
    season_year = y + as.integer(m == 12L))
}
period_indices <- function(index, period) {
  years <- ANNUAL_START_YEAR:ANALYSIS_END_YEAR
  ids <- lapply(years, function(y) {
    if (period == "Annual") which(index$year == y)
    else which(index$season == period & index$season_year == y)
  })
  assert_that(all(lengths(ids) == if (period == "Annual") 12L else 3L),
              paste("Incomplete monthly coverage for", period))
  ids
}
aggregate_series <- function(x, index, period) {
  assert_that(all(is.finite(x)), "Missing/non-finite monthly values: aggregation stopped.")
  vapply(period_indices(index, period), function(i) mean(x[i]), numeric(1))
}

# Stream a few months at a time. This retains all original metrics/maps without
# keeping five full 817-month global arrays in RAM simultaneously.
prepare_variable <- function(meta, variable, keep_map = FALSE) {
  nc <- ncdf4::nc_open(meta$path)
  on.exit(ncdf4::nc_close(nc), add = TRUE)
  ai <- which(meta$lat >= ARCTIC_LAT_THRESHOLD & meta$lat < 90)
  assert_that(length(ai) > 0, "No grid points in the Arctic domain.")
  weights <- matrix(cos(meta$lat[ai] * pi/180), length(ai), length(meta$lon))
  weighted <- unweighted <- coverage <- numeric(length(meta$dates))
  total <- matrix(0, length(meta$lat), length(meta$lon))
  counts <- total
  want_seasons <- keep_map && variable %in% c("eke_synoptic_mean", "eke_p95")
  seasonal_total <- setNames(lapply(SEASONS, function(s) total), SEASONS)
  seasonal_counts <- seasonal_total
  mi <- month_index(meta$dates)
  for (first in seq(1L, length(meta$dates), by = READ_MONTHS)) {
    n <- min(READ_MONTHS, length(meta$dates) - first + 1L)
    a <- read_cube(nc, variable, first, n)
    assert_that(!any(is.infinite(a)), paste("Infinite values in", variable))
    finite <- a[is.finite(a)]
    assert_that(length(finite) > 0 && min(finite) >= -1e-6,
                paste("Missing or negative energy/frequency in", variable))
    if (variable == "exceed_p95_freq")
      assert_that(max(finite) <= 1 + 1e-6, "Exceedance fractions exceed one.")
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      k <- first + j - 1L
      slice <- a[j, ai, , drop = FALSE]
      dim(slice) <- dim(weights)
      valid <- is.finite(slice)
      # A changing mask changes the region represented by a time series.
      # Stop rather than silently discard missing cells. ERA5 is expected complete.
      assert_that(all(valid), paste("Missing Arctic cells:", variable, meta$dates[k],
                                    "Check the input; no automatic preprocessing is run."))
      weighted[k] <- weighted.mean(slice, weights)
      unweighted[k] <- mean(slice)
      coverage[k] <- sum(weights[valid]) / sum(weights)
      if (want_seasons && mi$season_year[k] >= ANNUAL_START_YEAR &&
          mi$season_year[k] <= ANALYSIS_END_YEAR) {
        seas <- mi$season[k]; field <- a[j,,]; good <- is.finite(field)
        seasonal_total[[seas]][good] <- seasonal_total[[seas]][good] + field[good]
        seasonal_counts[[seas]][good] <- seasonal_counts[[seas]][good] + 1L
      }
      if (keep_map && meta$dates[k] >= as.Date(paste0(ANNUAL_START_YEAR, "-01-01"))) {
        field <- a[j, , ]; good <- is.finite(field)
        total[good] <- total[good] + field[good]
        counts[good] <- counts[good] + 1L
      }
    }
  }
  climatology <- total / counts
  climatology[counts == 0] <- NA_real_
  list(weighted = weighted, unweighted = unweighted, coverage = coverage,
       climatology = if (keep_map) climatology else NULL,
       seasonal_climatology = if (want_seasons) setNames(lapply(SEASONS, function(s) {
         x <- seasonal_total[[s]] / seasonal_counts[[s]]
         x[seasonal_counts[[s]] == 0] <- NA_real_
         x
       }), SEASONS) else NULL)
}
```

## 0.3 Shared statistical functions

`zhang_fit()` preserves the original `zyp.zhang()` settings and computes the
point estimate and PWMK p-value. It translates consecutive years to 1, 2, …,
which changes the origin but not the slope. Constant series return zero trend
and p = 1 explicitly.

`fit_with_mbb()` fits that same slope, computes a median intercept and
residuals, selects a block length from the residuals, resamples residual blocks,
adds back the fitted trend on the original years, and runs `zhang_fit()` again
in **every** replicate. The 2.5th and 97.5th bootstrap percentiles form an
approximate interval. `endcorr=TRUE` retains the original `tsboot()` default.

The interval assumes a useful linear-trend/residual model and approximately
stationary residual dependence. It is not an exact inversion of the PWMK test,
so disagreement between the CI and that test is exported for inspection. No
claim of guaranteed finite-sample coverage is made.

```{r statistical-helpers}
# One shared Zhang implementation: original point estimate and EVERY bootstrap
# replicate call this function, using the same yearly time axis and options.
zhang_fit <- function(y, years) {
  assert_that(length(y) == length(years) && length(y) >= 10L &&
                all(is.finite(y)) && all(is.finite(years)) && all(diff(years) == 1),
              "Zhang analysis requires finite observations on consecutive years.")
  if (length(unique(y)) == 1L)
    return(c(trend = 0, sig = 1, tau = 0, autocor = 0, nruns = 0))
  result <- zyp::zyp.zhang(y = y, x = years - years[1] + 1,
                          conf.intervals = FALSE,
                          preserve.range.for.sig.test = FALSE)
  assert_that(all(is.finite(result[c("trend", "sig", "tau")])) &&
                result["sig"] >= 0 && result["sig"] <= 1,
              "Zhang calculation returned an invalid slope or p-value.")
  result
}

get_block_length <- function(residuals) {
  # Select blocks from the residuals that will actually be resampled.
  # A trend in the original series should not determine residual block length.
  if (sd(residuals) < .Machine$double.eps)
    return(list(b = 1L, fallback = FALSE, reason = "constant residuals"))
  choice <- tryCatch({
    a <- blocklength::pwsd(residuals, round = TRUE, correlogram = FALSE)
    as.integer(a$BlockLength[1, "b_Circular"])
  }, error = function(e) NA_integer_)
  fallback <- length(choice) != 1L || !is.finite(choice) || choice < 1L ||
              choice >= length(residuals)
  list(b = if (fallback) B_FALLBACK else choice, fallback = fallback,
       reason = if (fallback) "PWSD unavailable or outside valid range" else "PWSD on residuals")
}

fit_with_mbb <- function(y, years, seed) {
  mk <- zhang_fit(y, years)
  beta <- unname(mk["trend"])
  t <- years - mean(years)
  center <- median(y - beta * t)
  residuals <- y - (center + beta * t)
  block <- get_block_length(residuals)
  # Percentile residual bootstrap: approximate intervals, conditional on the
  # fitted linear trend and residual dependence model. Not an exact MK inversion.
  set.seed(seed)
  replicate_count <- 0L
  ans <- boot::tsboot(
    tseries = residuals,
    statistic = function(r, ...) {
      # tsboot first evaluates the original residuals, then its replicates.
      replicate_count <<- replicate_count + 1L
      if (replicate_count > 1L && (replicate_count-1L) %% 250L == 0L) {
        cat("  Bootstrap replicates:",replicate_count-1L,"/",N_BOOT,"\n")
        flush.console()
      }
      y_star <- center + beta * t + as.numeric(r)
      unname(zhang_fit(y_star, years)["trend"])
    }, R = N_BOOT, l = block$b, sim = "fixed", endcorr = TRUE
  )
  draws <- as.numeric(ans$t)
  assert_that(length(draws) == N_BOOT && all(is.finite(draws)),
              "Bootstrap failed: invalid replicates are not silently discarded.")
  ci <- unname(quantile(draws, c(ALPHA/2, 1-ALPHA/2), type = 7))
  list(mk = mk, beta = beta, intercept = center - beta * mean(years),
       ci = ci, block = block, draws = draws,
       residual_rho1 = if (sd(residuals) > 0)
         as.numeric(acf(residuals, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]) else 0)
}

# BH is applied separately to each variable-period family. Missing tests are
# excluded explicitly. Rank one is sufficient, not necessary, for discoveries.
bh_field <- function(p, q = FDR_Q) {
  good <- is.finite(p)
  assert_that(all(p[good] >= 0 & p[good] <= 1), "Local p-values outside [0,1].")
  adjusted <- p * NA_real_
  if (any(good)) adjusted[good] <- p.adjust(p[good], method = "BH")
  list(p_bh = adjusted, sig_bh = adjusted <= q,
       n_tests = sum(good), n_discoveries = sum(adjusted <= q, na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

## 0.4 Small self-checks

These examples catch an end-of-month shift, incorrect DJF attribution, or an
incorrect BH implementation before the substantive calculations begin. The
second BH example demonstrates why the smallest p-value need not pass q/K:
a higher rank can trigger rejections.

```{r self-checks}
# These small checks test dates, season attribution and BH edge cases.
# They use synthetic inputs and do not read or change any ERA5 values.
a <- decode_months(c(0,31,59), "days since 1957-12-31 23:59:59.999999999")
assert_that(identical(as.character(a), c("1957-12-01","1958-01-01","1958-02-01")),
            "End-of-month decoding self-check failed.")
b <- decode_months(c(0,31*24,59*24), "hours since 1958-01-01 00:00:00")
assert_that(identical(as.character(b), c("1958-01-01","1958-02-01","1958-03-01")),
            "Hour-unit decoding self-check failed.")
i <- month_index(as.Date(c("1957-12-01","1958-01-01","1958-02-01")))
assert_that(all(i$season=="DJF" & i$season_year==1958), "DJF attribution self-check failed.")
# Higher ranks can trigger discoveries when rank one fails.
p <- c(0.0015,0.0016,rep(1,98))
assert_that(min(p) > 0.1/100 && bh_field(p,q=0.1)$n_discoveries==2,
            "BH step-up self-check failed.")
assert_that(bh_field(c(1.19e-7,rep(1,172799)),q=0.1)$n_discoveries>=1,
            "BH rank-one self-check failed.")
assert_that(bh_field(c(NA,0.5,0.9),q=0.1)$n_discoveries==0,
            "BH missing-value self-check failed.")
cat("Date, DJF and BH self-checks passed.\n")
```

# 1. Prepare and validate the monthly data

**Input:** four existing monthly NetCDFs. **Output:** `storm_df` (817 months),
`diagnostic_df` (816 calendar months), `annual_df` (68 years), `seasonal_df`
(68 observations per season), and small spatial climatology matrices.

A month key allows the energy files' month-end-at-midnight timestamps and the
storminess file's end-of-day timestamps to refer to the same month. Every file
must independently pass the coverage check before its values are combined.
Cosine weights account for shrinking cell areas towards the pole. Temporal
means retain the original equal-month weighting; no daily-weighting change is
introduced. The decomposition closure check is on the aligned domain means,
not a claim that every individual grid-cell residual has been checked.

The new preparation cache records file path, size, modification time, domain
and settings. This is a practical change detector, not a cryptographic audit of
all NetCDF values. If input contents change while metadata are deliberately
preserved, remove the corrected cache to rebuild it.

```{r prepare-monthly-data}
# Inspect the actual months and coordinates of all four inputs before loading data.
input_paths <- c(metrics = METRICS_FILE, tke = TKE_FILE,
                 mke = MKE_FILE, eke_budget = EKE_BUDGET_FILE)
metadata <- lapply(input_paths, read_metadata)
reference <- metadata$metrics
for (name in names(metadata)) {
  m <- metadata[[name]]
  assert_that(identical(m$dates, reference$dates), paste(name, "month mismatch"))
  assert_that(isTRUE(all.equal(m$lat, reference$lat)) &&
                isTRUE(all.equal(m$lon, reference$lon)), paste(name, "grid mismatch"))
}
lat <- reference$lat; lon <- reference$lon
lat_arctic <- lat[lat >= ARCTIC_LAT_THRESHOLD & lat < 90]
time_dates <- reference$dates
index <- month_index(time_dates)
years_vec <- ANNUAL_START_YEAR:ANALYSIS_END_YEAR

# A metadata table makes raw units, month decoding and file identity reviewable.
input_audit <- bind_rows(lapply(names(metadata), function(n) {
  m <- metadata[[n]]
  tibble(input = n, path = m$identity$path, bytes = m$identity$bytes,
    modified = m$identity$modified, time_units = m$time_units,
    calendar = m$calendar, n_months = length(m$dates),
    first_month = as.character(min(m$dates)), last_month = as.character(max(m$dates)),
    n_lat = length(m$lat), n_lon = length(m$lon))
}))
write_csv(input_audit, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Input_Audit.csv"))
print(knitr::kable(input_audit %>% select(input, n_months, first_month, last_month)))

prepare_signature <- object_hash(list(version = FRAMEWORK_VERSION,
  inputs = lapply(metadata, `[[`, "identity"), domain = ARCTIC_LAT_THRESHOLD,
  dates = time_dates, variables = ALL_VARS, climatology_start = ANNUAL_START_YEAR))
prepared_cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Prepared_Monthly.rds")
prepared <- if (file.exists(prepared_cache)) readRDS(prepared_cache) else NULL
if (is.null(prepared) || !identical(prepared$signature, prepare_signature)) {
  prepared <- list(signature = prepare_signature, variables = list())
  for (v in ALL_VARS) {
    cat("Reading and aggregating:", v, "\n")
    meta <- if (v %in% METRIC_NAMES) reference else metadata[[v]]
    prepared$variables[[v]] <- prepare_variable(meta, v, keep_map = v %in% METRIC_NAMES)
  }
  write_rds(prepared, prepared_cache)
} else cat("Reusing verified monthly preparation cache.\n")

storm_df <- index
for (v in ALL_VARS) storm_df[[v]] <- prepared$variables[[v]]$weighted
storm_df <- storm_df %>% mutate(eke_fraction = eke_budget/tke,
                               mke_eke_ratio = mke/eke_budget)
# All nonseasonal climatologies/diagnostics use Jan 1958--Dec 2025 (816 months).
# December 1957 is retained only in storm_df to complete DJF 1958.
diagnostic_df <- storm_df %>% filter(year >= ANNUAL_START_YEAR, year <= ANALYSIS_END_YEAR)
climatology_maps_full <- lapply(prepared$variables[METRIC_NAMES], `[[`, "climatology")

ts_start <- c(ANNUAL_START_YEAR, 1)
ts_objects <- lapply(diagnostic_df[METRIC_NAMES], ts, start = ts_start, frequency = 12)
deseasonalize <- function(df, metric_col) {
  df[[metric_col]] - ave(df[[metric_col]], df$month, FUN = mean)
}
ts_objects_anom <- lapply(METRIC_NAMES, function(v)
  ts(deseasonalize(diagnostic_df, v), start = ts_start, frequency = 12))
names(ts_objects_anom) <- METRIC_NAMES
ts_objects_energy_anom <- lapply(ENERGY_VARS, function(v)
  ts(deseasonalize(diagnostic_df, v), start = ts_start, frequency = 12))
names(ts_objects_energy_anom) <- ENERGY_VARS

annual_df <- tibble(year = years_vec)
for (v in ALL_VARS) annual_df[[v]] <- aggregate_series(storm_df[[v]], index, "Annual")
seasonal_df <- bind_rows(lapply(SEASONS, function(seas) {
  out <- tibble(season = seas, season_year = years_vec)
  for (v in ALL_VARS) out[[v]] <- aggregate_series(storm_df[[v]], index, seas)
  out
}))
energy_annual <- annual_df %>% mutate(eke_fraction = eke_budget/tke, mke_eke_ratio = mke/eke_budget)
# Keep the original definition for annual means of monthly partition ratios.
for (v in c("eke_fraction", "mke_eke_ratio"))
  energy_annual[[v]] <- aggregate_series(storm_df[[v]], index, "Annual")

budget_residual <- diagnostic_df$tke - diagnostic_df$mke - diagnostic_df$eke_budget
relative_error <- 100 * mean(abs(budget_residual)) / mean(diagnostic_df$tke)
budget_audit <- tibble(date = diagnostic_df$date, residual = budget_residual,
                       relative_error_pct = 100*abs(budget_residual)/diagnostic_df$tke)
write_csv(budget_audit, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Energy_Budget_Closure.csv"))
assert_that(is.finite(relative_error) && relative_error < 0.01,
            "Mean energy closure error exceeds 0.01%; inspect the aligned input files.")
cat(sprintf("Domain-mean closure error: %.8f%%\n", relative_error))
write_csv(storm_df, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "storm_metrics_panarctic_monthly.csv"))
write_csv(annual_df, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Annual_Means.csv"))
write_csv(seasonal_df, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Seasonal_Means.csv"))
```

# 2. Understand variability before interpreting trends

## 2.1 Descriptive statistics and monthly autocorrelation

The anomalies subtract the 1958–2025 calendar-month climatology. ACF measures
correlation across lags; PACF conditions on intermediate lags. Neither a
nonzero lag-one correlation nor a PACF plot alone proves an AR(1) model.

The retained `neff_positive_24lag` calculation clips negative sample ACFs to
zero. It is explicitly a **descriptive heuristic**, not an exact effective
sample size or a correction applied to the trend tests. Its definition must
match any formula or numbers used in the thesis.

In the preprocessing source, the fixed 1961–1990 P95 threshold is estimated
from every fourth six-hourly sample (one sample per day); monthly exceedances
use all six-hourly samples. Therefore the equally weighted monthly reference
mean need not equal precisely 5%. Exceedance is the fraction of sampled times
above the threshold, not a count of distinct storms. Monthly local P90/P95/P99
values are averaged spatially/seasonally, not recomputed as pooled quantiles.

```{r descriptive-diagnostics}
# These diagnostics describe monthly variability. Their n_eff values are NOT
# used as sample sizes or degrees of freedom in the annual/seasonal trend tests.
diagnostic_rows <- lapply(ALL_VARS, function(v) {
  x <- diagnostic_df[[v]]
  a <- deseasonalize(diagnostic_df, v)
  rho <- as.numeric(acf(a, lag.max = 24, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]
  N <- length(a); k <- seq_along(rho)
  # Retain the original positive-clipped 24-lag diagnostic, naming it explicitly.
  # Clipping noisy negative estimates is a heuristic, not an exact IAT estimator.
  neff_positive <- N/(1 + 2*sum((1-k/N)*pmax(rho, 0)))
  tibble(variable = v, N = N, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), min = min(x), max = max(x),
         rho1_raw = as.numeric(acf(x, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]),
         rho1_anomaly = rho[1], neff_positive_24lag = neff_positive)
})
summary_stats <- bind_rows(diagnostic_rows)
write_csv(summary_stats, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Descriptive_Statistics.csv"))
print(knitr::kable(summary_stats, digits = 4))

# Annual and seasonal climatologies use complete years/seasons, including
# Dec 1957 in DJF 1958 but excluding Dec 2025 from the incomplete DJF 2026.
climatology_table <- bind_rows(
  annual_df %>% summarise(across(all_of(ALL_VARS), mean)) %>% mutate(period = "Annual"),
  seasonal_df %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(across(all_of(ALL_VARS), mean), .groups="drop") %>%
    rename(period = season)
) %>% select(period, all_of(ALL_VARS))
write_csv(climatology_table, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Annual_Seasonal_Climatology.csv"))
print(knitr::kable(climatology_table, digits = 3))

ref <- diagnostic_df %>% filter(year >= REFERENCE_PERIOD[1], year <= REFERENCE_PERIOD[2])
cat(sprintf("Reference mean exceedance fraction: %.6f\n", mean(ref$exceed_p95_freq)))
cat("This need not equal exactly 0.05: the threshold used one sample/day,\n",
    "exceedances use four/day, and months receive equal weight.\n")

# A reusable plot function converts ts objects to numeric vectors so lag 12
# really means 12 MONTHS on the ACF/PACF axes, not one year labelled as a month.
plot_acf_pair <- function(objects, path, colours) {
  png(path, width = 12, height = 2.7*length(objects), units = "in", res = 300)
  on.exit(dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  par(mfrow = c(length(objects), 2), mar = c(4,4,3,1), oma = c(0,0,2,0))
  for (v in names(objects)) {
    a <- as.numeric(objects[[v]])
    acf(a, lag.max = 36, xlab = "Lag (months)", main = paste("ACF:", VAR_LABELS_PLAIN[v]),
        col = colours[v], lwd = 2)
    pacf(a, lag.max = 36, xlab = "Lag (months)", main = paste("PACF:", VAR_LABELS_PLAIN[v]),
         col = colours[v], lwd = 2)
  }
  mtext("Monthly anomalies, January 1958--December 2025", outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
}
```

## 2.4 STL decomposition

STL separates a periodic seasonal component, a smooth trend and a remainder.
The trend is a descriptive smooth component, not an attributed externally
forced climate response. Component variance / observed variance ratios need
not sum to 100%, because covariance terms also enter the variance identity.

```{r stl-decomposition}
# PLOT 5: STL DECOMPOSITION
# ============================================================================

cat("\n--- Generating Plot 5: STL Decomposition ---\n")

# STL decomposition for primary metric (eke_synoptic_mean)
stl_result <- stl(ts_objects$eke_synoptic_mean, s.window = "periodic")

# Extract components
stl_df <- data.frame(
  date = plot_dates,
  observed = as.vector(ts_objects$eke_synoptic_mean),
  seasonal = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "seasonal"]),
  trend = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "trend"]),
  remainder = as.vector(stl_result$time.series[, "remainder"])
)

# Calculate component contributions
var_total <- var(stl_df$observed, na.rm = TRUE)
var_seasonal <- var(stl_df$seasonal, na.rm = TRUE)
var_trend <- var(stl_df$trend, na.rm = TRUE)
var_remainder <- var(stl_df$remainder, na.rm = TRUE)

pct_seasonal <- (var_seasonal / var_total) * 100
pct_trend <- (var_trend / var_total) * 100
pct_remainder <- (var_remainder / var_total) * 100

cat(sprintf("  Component/observed variance ratios:\n"))
cat(sprintf("    Seasonal: %.1f%%\n", pct_seasonal))
cat(sprintf("    Trend:    %.1f%%\n", pct_trend))
cat(sprintf("    Residual: %.1f%%\n", pct_remainder))

# Create STL plot
stl_long <- stl_df %>%
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    component = factor(component, 
                       levels = c("observed", "seasonal", "trend", "remainder")),
    component_label = case_when(
      component == "observed" ~ sprintf("Observed Data"),
      component == "seasonal" ~ sprintf("Seasonal (%.1f%% variance ratio)", pct_seasonal),
      component == "trend" ~ sprintf("Trend (%.1f%% variance ratio)", pct_trend),
      component == "remainder" ~ sprintf("Remainder (%.1f%% variance ratio)", pct_remainder)
    ),
    component_label = factor(component_label, levels = unique(component_label))
  )

p5 <- ggplot(stl_long, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ component_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = parse(text = paste0('bold("STL Decomposition: "~', VAR_LABELS_SHORT[["eke_synoptic_mean"]], '~"(Primary Metric)")'))[[1]],
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N) | Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS",
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("m"^2*"/s"^2)
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = TITLE_SIZE),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

if (MAKE_FIGURES) ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig05_STL_Decomposition.png"),
       p5, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

# Also save STL for P95 (extreme intensity)
stl_p95 <- stl(ts_objects$eke_p95, s.window = "periodic")

stl_p95_df <- data.frame(
  date = plot_dates,
  observed = as.vector(ts_objects$eke_p95),
  seasonal = as.vector(stl_p95$time.series[, "seasonal"]),
  trend = as.vector(stl_p95$time.series[, "trend"]),
  remainder = as.vector(stl_p95$time.series[, "remainder"])
)

# Store for later use
stl_results <- list(
  eke_synoptic_mean = stl_result,
  eke_p95 = stl_p95
)

# ============================================================================

write_csv(stl_df,file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR,"STL_Components.csv"))
stl_variance <- tibble(component=c("seasonal","trend","remainder"),
  variance=c(var_seasonal,var_trend,var_remainder),
  ratio_pct=c(pct_seasonal,pct_trend,pct_remainder))
write_csv(stl_variance,file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR,"STL_Variance_Ratios.csv"))
cat("Sum of variance ratios:",sum(stl_variance$ratio_pct),"%; covariance terms are not included.\n")
```

## 2.5 Spatial climatologies

These plots retain the original map suite and use the full input latitude
extent for context (normally 55°N–89.75°N). Numerical domain means and trend
maps use ≥60°N. Climatology grids were already accumulated in Stage 1, so this
stage does not load five full monthly cubes. Separate panels may use different
colour scales; the four seasons of each variable share one scale.

P95/mean is a descriptive ratio. It does not by itself identify a heavy-tailed
probability distribution. The seasonal climatologies include only complete
1958–2025 seasons.

```{r climatology-map-01}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# STEP 1: CREATE A SPATIALLY-AWARE `stars` OBJECT (WITH WRAPPING)
# ============================================================================

# 1. Prepare Longitude Vector with Wrapping
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We extend the longitude vector by one point to close the gap at 180 deg
lon_vec <- as.vector(lon)
lat_vec <- as.vector(lat) 

# Create a new longitude vector that adds one point (start + 360)
lon_wrapped <- c(lon_vec, lon_vec[1] + 360)

cat(sprintf("  Wrapping longitude: Original %d points -> Wrapped %d points\n", 
            length(lon_vec), length(lon_wrapped)))

# 2. Helper function to wrap matrices
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Input: [lat, lon] matrix
# Output: [lon_wrapped, lat] matrix
wrap_data <- function(mat) {
  # Transpose to [lon, lat]
  mat_t <- t(mat)
  # Append the first row (first longitude) to the end
  mat_wrapped <- rbind(mat_t, mat_t[1, ])
  return(mat_wrapped)
}

# 3. Create Wrapped Data List
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
data_list_plot <- list(
  eke_synoptic_mean = wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$eke_synoptic_mean),
  eke_p90           = wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$eke_p90),
  eke_p95           = wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$eke_p95),
  eke_p99           = wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$eke_p99),
  exceed_freq       = wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$exceed_p95_freq)
)

# 4. Create Dimensions and Stars Object
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IMPORTANT: Use 'lon_wrapped' here, not the original 'lon_vec'
dims <- st_dimensions(x = lon_wrapped, y = lat_vec)

# Create the stars object and set CRS
clim_stars <- st_as_stars(data_list_plot, dimensions = dims) %>%
  st_set_crs(4326)

cat("  Stars object created (gap repaired)\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: REPROJECT ALL SPATIAL DATA
# ============================================================================

# Define the target projection: Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area, centered on North Pole
arctic_crs <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +lon_0=0"

# Warp the raster data to polar projection
clim_polar <- st_warp(clim_stars, crs = arctic_crs)

# Load and transform coastlines
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
world_polar <- st_transform(world, crs = arctic_crs)

cat("  Data reprojected to polar CRS\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: CREATE CARTOGRAPHIC ELEMENTS
# ============================================================================

# Define two radii for "two-ring" masking approach
view_radius <- 3700000  # 3700 km - data boundary
plot_radius <- 4400000  # 4400 km - space for labels

# Create circular mask
circle_mask <- st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = arctic_crs) %>%
  st_buffer(dist = view_radius)

# Apply mask to data
clim_polar_masked <- clim_polar[circle_mask]

# Create inverse mask (square with circular hole)
square_box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -plot_radius, xmax = plot_radius,
  ymin = -plot_radius, ymax = plot_radius
), crs = arctic_crs))
inverse_mask <- st_difference(square_box, circle_mask)

# Create graticule lines
graticules <- st_graticule(
  lon = seq(-180, 180, by = 60),
  lat = c(60, 70, 80),
  crs = 4326
) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)

# Create latitude labels (positioned at 180° longitude for visibility)
lat_labels <- data.frame(
  lon = 180,
  lat = c(60, 70, 80)
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lat_labels$label <- c("60°N", "70°N", "80°N")

# Create longitude labels (positioned in the blank space between radii)
lon_labels <- data.frame(
  lon = seq(0, 300, by = 60),
  lat = 54  # Falls in blank space between view_radius and plot_radius
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = arctic_crs)
lon_labels$label <- c("0°", "60°E", "120°E", "180°", "120°W", "60°W")

cat("  Cartographic elements created\n")

# ==========================================================================
# STEP 4: Compute derived fields
# ==========================================================================

# --- 0a. Per-group colour limits (each figure section uses its own scale) ---
# Fig 6a: EKE_synoptic + P95 share one scale
syn_p95_max    <- ceiling(max(
  max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_synoptic_mean"]], na.rm = TRUE),
  max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_p95"]],           na.rm = TRUE)
) / 10) * 10
syn_p95_breaks <- seq(0, syn_p95_max, length.out = 5)

# Fig 6b: P90 independent scale
p90_max    <- ceiling(max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_p90"]], na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
p90_breaks <- seq(0, p90_max, length.out = 5)

# Fig 6c: P99 independent scale
p99_max    <- ceiling(max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_p99"]], na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
p99_breaks <- seq(0, p99_max, length.out = 5)

# Standalone individual scales (each variable on its own range)
syn_max        <- ceiling(max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_synoptic_mean"]], na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
syn_breaks     <- seq(0, syn_max, length.out = 5)

p95_max        <- ceiling(max(clim_polar_masked[["eke_p95"]], na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
p95_breaks     <- seq(0, p95_max, length.out = 5)

cat(sprintf("  EKE_synoptic + P95 shared limits: [0, %d] | breaks: %s\n",
            syn_p95_max, paste(syn_p95_breaks, collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("  P90 limits: [0, %d] | breaks: %s\n",
            p90_max, paste(p90_breaks, collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("  P99 limits: [0, %d] | breaks: %s\n",
            p99_max, paste(p99_breaks, collapse = ", ")))

# --- 0b. Compute P95/Mean ratio and rebuild stars object ---
climatology_maps_full[["p95_mean_ratio"]] <-
  climatology_maps_full$eke_p95 / climatology_maps_full$eke_synoptic_mean

# Add wrapped ratio to data list
data_list_plot[["p95_mean_ratio"]] <- wrap_data(climatology_maps_full$p95_mean_ratio)

# Rebuild stars object with the extra attribute
dims <- st_dimensions(x = lon_wrapped, y = lat_vec)

clim_stars <- st_as_stars(data_list_plot, dimensions = dims) %>%
  st_set_crs(4326)

clim_polar        <- st_warp(clim_stars, crs = arctic_crs)
clim_polar_masked <- clim_polar[circle_mask]

ratio_range  <- range(clim_polar_masked[["p95_mean_ratio"]], na.rm = TRUE)
median_ratio <- median(clim_polar_masked[["p95_mean_ratio"]], na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("  P95/Mean ratio — median: %.2f, range: [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
            median_ratio, ratio_range[1], ratio_range[2]))
```

```{r climatology-map-02}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# FIGURE 6a: MEAN EKE + P95 EKE (1×2, shared colourbar, 5 ticks)
# ==========================================================================
cat("\n--- Generating Figure 6a: Spatial Climatology Mean EKE + P95 EKE ---\n")

# Helper: shared theme for every panel in this figure
panel_theme <- theme_void(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = TITLE_SIZE),
    legend.position   = "right",
    legend.key.width  = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(2.0, "cm"),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 15, 10, 15)
  )

eke_scale_syn <- scale_fill_viridis(
  name     = expression(atop("EKE", "[m"^2*"/s"^2*"]")),
  option   = "C",
  na.value = "transparent",
  limits   = c(0, syn_max),
  breaks   = syn_breaks,
  oob      = scales::squish
)

eke_scale_p95_fig6a <- scale_fill_viridis(
  name     = expression(atop("EKE", "[m"^2*"/s"^2*"]")),
  option   = "C",
  na.value = "transparent",
  limits   = c(0, p95_max),
  breaks   = p95_breaks,
  oob      = scales::squish
)

eke_scale_p90 <- scale_fill_viridis(
  name     = expression(atop("EKE", "[m"^2*"/s"^2*"]")),
  option   = "C",
  na.value = "transparent",
  limits   = c(0, p90_max),
  breaks   = p90_breaks,
  oob      = scales::squish
)

eke_scale_p99 <- scale_fill_viridis(
  name     = expression(atop("EKE", "[m"^2*"/s"^2*"]")),
  option   = "C",
  na.value = "transparent",
  limits   = c(0, p99_max),
  breaks   = p99_breaks,
  oob      = scales::squish
)

# --- Panel (a): Mean EKE ---
p6a_mean <- ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = clim_polar_masked, aes(fill = eke_synoptic_mean), na.rm = TRUE) +
  eke_scale_syn +
  geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label),
               size = 2.5, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
  geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label),
               size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius),
           ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = parse(text = paste0('bold("(a) "~', VAR_LABELS_SHORT[["eke_synoptic_mean"]], ')'))[[1]]) +
  panel_theme

# --- Panel (b): P95 EKE ---
p6a_p95 <- ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = clim_polar_masked, aes(fill = eke_p95), na.rm = TRUE) +
  eke_scale_p95_fig6a +
  geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label),
               size = 2.5, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
  geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label),
               size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius),
           ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = parse(text = paste0('bold("(b) "~', VAR_LABELS_SHORT[["eke_p95"]], ')'))[[1]]) +
  panel_theme

fig6a <- (p6a_mean | p6a_p95) +
  plot_layout() +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Spatial Climatology of EKE (1958–2025)",
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥55°N) | Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Independent colour scales",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = TITLE_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = SUBTITLE_SIZE, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  )

print(fig6a)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig06a_EKE_Synoptic_P95_Climatology.png"),
       fig6a, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

```{r climatology-map-06}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# STANDALONE INDIVIDUAL FIGURES (each variable, own colourbar)
# ==========================================================================
# Each panel is rebuilt with its own independent scale so the colourbar
# reflects that variable's own data range, not the shared Fig06a range.
cat("\n--- Generating standalone individual spatial climatology figures ---\n")

make_standalone <- function(fill_var, scale_obj, label_expr) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_stars(data = clim_polar_masked, aes(fill = .data[[fill_var]]), na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_obj +
    geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +

      title    = parse(text = paste0("bold(", label_expr, ")"))[[1]],
      subtitle = "Spatial Climatology (1958–2025) | Pan-Arctic (≥55°N)"
    ) +

}
```

```{r climatology-map-07}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# FIGURE 6d: SEASONAL SPATIAL CLIMATOLOGY (2×2: DJF, MAM, JJA, SON)
# ==========================================================================
cat("\n--- Generating Figure 6d: Seasonal Spatial Climatology (Mean EKE) ---\n")

# Use Stage 1 climatologies from 68 complete seasons.


seasonal_clim_maps <- prepared$variables$eke_synoptic_mean$seasonal_climatology

# --- 2. Build stars objects for each season (wrap → project → mask) ---
season_panels_clim <- list()

# Shared colour limits across all four seasons
seas_vals <- unlist(lapply(seasonal_clim_maps, function(m) {
  wrapped <- wrap_data(m)
  s <- st_as_stars(list(eke = wrapped),
                   dimensions = st_dimensions(x = lon_wrapped, y = lat_vec)) %>%
    st_set_crs(4326)
  sp <- st_warp(s, crs = arctic_crs)
  sm <- sp[circle_mask]
  as.vector(sm[["eke"]])
}))
seas_max    <- ceiling(max(seas_vals, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
seas_breaks <- seq(0, seas_max, length.out = 5)

cat(sprintf("  Shared seasonal colour limits: [0, %d]\n", seas_max))

eke_scale_seasonal <- function() {
  scale_fill_viridis(
    name     = expression(atop("EKE", "[m"^2*"/s"^2*"]")),
    option   = "C",
    na.value = "transparent",
    limits   = c(0, seas_max),
    breaks   = seas_breaks,
    oob      = scales::squish
  )
}

for (seas in SEASONS) {
  # Wrap, create stars, project, mask
  mat_w  <- wrap_data(seasonal_clim_maps[[seas]])
  s_star <- st_as_stars(list(eke = mat_w),
                        dimensions = st_dimensions(x = lon_wrapped, y = lat_vec)) %>%
    st_set_crs(4326)
  s_polar  <- st_warp(s_star, crs = arctic_crs)
  s_masked <- s_polar[circle_mask]

  season_panels_clim[[seas]] <- ggplot() +
    geom_stars(data = s_masked, aes(fill = eke), na.rm = TRUE) +
    eke_scale_seasonal() +
    geom_sf(data = world_polar, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = graticules, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_sf(data = inverse_mask, fill = "white", color = NA) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lat_labels, aes(label = label),
                 size = 2.5, color = "black", hjust = 1.2) +
    geom_sf_text(data = lon_labels, aes(label = label),
                 size = 2.5, color = "black") +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius),
             ylim = c(-plot_radius, plot_radius), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = SEASON_NAMES[seas]) +
    panel_theme
}

# --- 3. Apply horizontal bottom legend to each panel (S7-safe) ---
legend_style_clim <- theme(
  legend.direction      = "horizontal",
  legend.title.position = "top",
  legend.title          = element_text(size = BASE_SIZE, hjust = 0.5),
  legend.key.width      = unit(3.0, "cm"),
  legend.key.height     = unit(0.5, "cm")
)
legend_guide_clim <- guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top",
                                                   title.hjust = 0.5))

for (seas in names(season_panels_clim)) {
  season_panels_clim[[seas]] <- season_panels_clim[[seas]] +
    legend_style_clim + legend_guide_clim
}

# --- 4. Combine 2×2 + guide_area (same pattern as Phase 3 seasonal maps) ---
fig6d <- (season_panels_clim[["DJF"]] + season_panels_clim[["MAM"]] +
            season_panels_clim[["JJA"]] + season_panels_clim[["SON"]] +
            guide_area()) +
  plot_layout(design = "AB\nCD\nEE", guides = "collect",
              heights = c(1, 1, 0.15)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = parse(text = 'bold("Seasonal Spatial Climatology of "~"Mean EKE"[synoptic]~"(1958–2025)")')[[1]],
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥55°N) | Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area Projection | Shared colour scale",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = TITLE_SIZE, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = SUBTITLE_SIZE, colour = "grey40",
                                   hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10))
    )
  )

print(fig6d)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig06d_Seasonal_Climatology_EKE.png"),
       fig6d, width = 14, height = 15, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

rm(season_panels_clim, seasonal_clim_maps, seas_vals, fig6d)
gc(verbose = FALSE)
```

## 2.6 Distributions, metric correlations and period composites

Monthly correlations include a shared seasonal cycle, so they do not prove
that anomalies or long-term trends covary. The period composites retain the
original bins: 1958–1969 contains 12 years and 2020–2025 contains six. Their
labels now match the data, and December 1957 is excluded from these calendar
composites. They are descriptive comparisons, not a homogeneity test.

```{r distribution-plot-01}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES

```

```{r distribution-plot-02}
# Prepare data
dist_data <- storm_df %>%
  select(all_of(METRICS)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = METRICS))

p7 <- ggplot(dist_data, aes(x = value, fill = metric)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50, alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  geom_density(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free", ncol = 3,
             labeller = as_labeller(VAR_LABELS, default = label_parsed)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(

    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N) | 1958–2025 | n = 816 months",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = TITLE_SIZE),
```

```{r distribution-plot-03}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# PLOT 8: METRIC CORRELATION MATRIX
# ============================================================================

cat("\n--- Generating Plot 8: Correlation Matrix ---\n")

# Calculate correlation matrix — keep METRICS as row/col names so downstream
# indexing (cat/sprintf below) uses clean variable keys, not display strings.
cor_data <- storm_df %>%
  select(all_of(METRICS))

cor_matrix <- cor(cor_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
rownames(cor_matrix) <- METRICS
colnames(cor_matrix) <- METRICS

# Build plotmath axis labels from VAR_LABELS_SHORT (setup chunk).
# parse() returns an expression object; scale_x/y_discrete(labels=) accepts
# a named vector of expressions to render each level as plotmath.
cor_axis_labels <- setNames(
  parse(text = VAR_LABELS_SHORT[METRICS]),
  METRICS
)

# Melt to long format and keep upper triangle (including diagonal)
cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  rename(row_var = Var1, col_var = Var2, correlation = Freq) %>%
  mutate(
    row_var = factor(row_var, levels = METRICS),
    col_var = factor(col_var, levels = METRICS)
  ) %>%
  filter(as.integer(row_var) <= as.integer(col_var))

p8 <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = col_var, y = fct_rev(row_var), fill = correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)), size = 3.5, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = cor_axis_labels) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = cor_axis_labels) +
  labs(
    title    = "Correlation Between Storminess Metrics",
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N) | 1958–2025",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
    axis.text.y   = element_text(hjust = 1),
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid    = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig08_Correlation_Matrix.png"),
       p8, width = 11, height = 9, dpi = 300)

# Print correlation summary
cat("\n  Correlation matrix:\n")
print(round(cor_matrix, 3))

# ============================================================================
```

```{r distribution-plot-04}
cat("\n--- Generating Plot 9: Anomaly Time Series ---\n")

# Calculate anomalies (remove seasonal cycle)
storm_df_anom <- storm_df %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  mutate(
    eke_synoptic_mean_anom = eke_synoptic_mean - mean(eke_synoptic_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    eke_p95_anom = eke_p95 - mean(eke_p95, na.rm = TRUE),

# Plot anomalies
```

```{r distribution-plot-05}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# PLOT 10: SEASONAL CYCLE BY DECADE (STABILITY CHECK)
# ============================================================================

cat("\n--- Generating Plot 10: Seasonal Cycle Stability ---\n")

# Create decade labels
storm_df_decade <- storm_df %>%
  mutate(
    decade = case_when(
      year >= 1958 & year < 1970 ~ "1958-1969",  # 12 calendar years
      year >= 1970 & year < 1980 ~ "1970-1979",
      year >= 1980 & year < 1990 ~ "1980-1989",
      year >= 1990 & year < 2000 ~ "1990-1999",
      year >= 2000 & year < 2010 ~ "2000-2009",
      year >= 2010 & year < 2020 ~ "2010-2019",
      year >= 2020              ~ "2020-2025"
    ),
    decade = factor(decade, levels = c(
      "1958-1969", "1970-1979", "1980-1989", "1990-1999",
      "2000-2009", "2010-2019", "2020-2025"
    ))
  )

# Calculate seasonal cycle by decade
seasonal_by_decade <- storm_df_decade %>%
  group_by(decade, month) %>%
  summarise(
    eke_synoptic_mean_avg = mean(eke_synoptic_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    eke_synoptic_mean_se = sd(eke_synoptic_mean, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# We will use the built-in viridis scale inside the plot.
p10 <- ggplot(seasonal_by_decade, aes(x = month, y = eke_synoptic_mean_avg, 
                                      color = decade, group = decade)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  
  # 'end = 0.9' prevents the lines from becoming too yellow/invisible
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Decade", end = 0.9) +
  
  labs(
    title = parse(text = paste0('bold("Evolution of the Seasonal Cycle: "~', VAR_LABELS_SHORT[["eke_synoptic_mean"]], ')'))[[1]],
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N) | Has the seasonal pattern changed over time?",
    x = NULL,
    y = parse(text = VAR_LABELS[["eke_synoptic_mean"]])[[1]]
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = TITLE_SIZE),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig10_Seasonal_Cycle_ByDecade.png"),
       p10, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# Also create for exceedance frequency 
seasonal_exceed_decade <- storm_df_decade %>%
  group_by(decade, month) %>%
  summarise(
    exceed_avg = mean(exceed_p95_freq, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p10b <- ggplot(seasonal_exceed_decade, aes(x = month, y = exceed_avg, 
                                           color = decade, group = decade)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  
  # --- MODIFICATION: Apply the same scale to the second plot ---
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Decade", end = 0.9) +
  
  labs(
    title = parse(text = paste0('bold("Evolution of the Seasonal Cycle: "~', VAR_LABELS_SHORT[["exceed_p95_freq"]], ')'))[[1]],
    subtitle = "Pan-Arctic (≥60°N) | Dashed line = 5% reference frequency",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Exceedance Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = BASE_SIZE) +
```

# 3. Describe the energy partition

These are descriptive comparisons of existing monthly products. Budget EKE
uses deviations from each month's mean and satisfies TKE = MKE + EKE.
Synoptic EKE uses bandpass-filtered winds. Their ratio is not an exact
partition into complementary frequency bands, and correlation does not
establish identical trends or an energy-transfer mechanism.

```{r energy-plot-context}
fig_dir <- FIG_PHASE2
```


```{r energy-figure-2}

# ============================================================================
# Key question: how does the energy budget vary by month?
#

#   - TKE and EKE peak in winter (DJF), trough in summer (JJA)

            winter_eke, summer_eke, winter_eke / summer_eke))
cat(sprintf("  MKE:        winter = %.1f, summer = %.1f m²/s² (ratio: %.2f)\n",
            winter_mke, summer_mke, winter_mke / summer_mke))
```

# 4. Estimate annual and seasonal Pan-Arctic trends

## 4.1 Calculate estimates and matching intervals

There are eight annual series and 32 seasonal series. Within this code, the
Zhang slope is the Sen-based slope returned by the iterative Zhang procedure;
it is not labelled as the unmodified median of all raw-data pairwise slopes. The significance column
uses the **unrounded nominal PWMK p-value**. Calculations and CSVs retain full
precision; rounding is only for display. `pct_change` is fitted change over
67 years divided by that series' mean, expressed as a percentage. For
exceedance frequency, `exceed_pp_dec` also reports percentage points per decade.

Each result is cached separately against its series, settings, seed, R version
and statistical package versions. Rerunning after an interruption reuses
completed compatible calculations. A change in N_BOOT or the input values
invalidates the affected cache. Old result tables, if present, are joined only
for a previous-versus-corrected comparison; they never supply current estimates.

These tests do not attribute changes to sea ice or other causes. Seasonal
results are nominal unless a family correction is explicitly applied; five
correlated metrics are not five independent confirmations. Significance in
one season and nonsignificance in another is not a test of their difference.

```{r annual-and-seasonal-trends}
# A cache is tied to actual series values, settings, and package versions.
# Old confidence intervals are never reused because their estimator differed.
trend_row <- function(x, years, variable, period, seed) {
  signature <- object_hash(list(schema = "zhang-residual-mbb-v1", framework = FRAMEWORK_VERSION, x = x, years = years,
    N_BOOT = N_BOOT, alpha = ALPHA, fallback = B_FALLBACK, seed = seed,
    R = as.character(getRversion()),
    packages = vapply(c("zyp", "blocklength", "boot"),
                      function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))))
  path <- file.path(TREND_CACHE_DIR, paste0(period, "__", variable, ".rds"))
  old <- if (file.exists(path)) readRDS(path) else NULL
  if (!FORCE_TREND_RECOMPUTE && !is.null(old) && identical(old$signature, signature)) {
    fit <- old$fit
    cat("Reusing:", period, variable, "\n")
  } else {
    cat("Calculating:", period, variable, "with", N_BOOT, "bootstrap replicates\n")
    flush.console()
    fit <- fit_with_mbb(x, years, seed)
    write_rds(list(signature = signature, fit = fit), path)
  }
  average <- mean(x)
  total_change <- fit$beta * diff(range(years))
  tibble(period = period, variable = variable,
    label = unname(VAR_LABELS_PLAIN[variable]),
    group = ifelse(variable %in% METRIC_NAMES, "Storminess", "Energy"),
    n = length(x), mean_val = average, slope_dec = fit$beta*DECADES,
    ci_lower = fit$ci[1]*DECADES, ci_upper = fit$ci[2]*DECADES,
    intercept = fit$intercept, tau = unname(fit$mk["tau"]),
    p_value = unname(fit$mk["sig"]), ar1_removed = unname(fit$mk["autocor"]),
    nruns = unname(fit$mk["nruns"]), significant = unname(fit$mk["sig"]) < ALPHA,
    pct_change = if (average != 0) 100*total_change/average else NA_real_,
    total_change = total_change,
    exceed_pp_dec = if (variable == "exceed_p95_freq") fit$beta*DECADES*100 else NA_real_,
    b_length = fit$block$b, block_fallback = fit$block$fallback,
    block_reason = fit$block$reason, residual_rho1 = fit$residual_rho1,
    bootstrap_seed = seed, bootstrap_R = N_BOOT)
}
results_annual <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(ALL_VARS), function(i) {
  v <- ALL_VARS[i]
  trend_row(annual_df[[v]], annual_df$year, v, "Annual", BOOT_SEED+i)
}))
write_csv(results_annual, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Annual_Trends_FullPrecision.csv"))
print(knitr::kable(results_annual %>% select(label, slope_dec, ci_lower, ci_upper,
                                           p_value, pct_change, b_length), digits = 5))

results_seasonal <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(SEASONS), function(j) {
  seas <- SEASONS[j]
  d <- seasonal_df %>% filter(season == seas)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(ALL_VARS), function(i) {
    v <- ALL_VARS[i]
    trend_row(d[[v]], d$season_year, v, seas, BOOT_SEED+j*100L+i)
  }))
})) %>% mutate(season = factor(period, levels = SEASONS))
write_csv(results_seasonal, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "Seasonal_Trends_FullPrecision.csv"))
print(knitr::kable(results_seasonal %>% select(season, label, slope_dec, ci_lower,
  ci_upper, p_value, pct_change, b_length), digits = 5))

# Export any disagreement between two different inferential procedures rather
# than silently treating a bootstrap CI as the inverse of the PWMK test.
ci_test_comparison <- bind_rows(results_annual, results_seasonal) %>%
  mutate(ci_excludes_zero = ci_lower > 0 | ci_upper < 0,
         ci_pwmk_disagree = ci_excludes_zero != significant)
write_csv(ci_test_comparison, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, "CI_and_PWMK_Comparison.csv"))

# Compare to old tables only for audit; old values never enter calculations.
compare_old_results <- function(path, object, new, keys) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(invisible(NULL))
  e <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  load(path, envir = e)
  if (!exists(object, envir = e, inherits = FALSE)) return(invisible(NULL))
  old <- get(object, envir = e)
  cols <- c(keys, "slope_dec", "p_value", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "pct_change")
  if (!all(cols %in% names(old))) return(invisible(NULL))
  comparison <- full_join(select(new, all_of(cols)), select(old, all_of(cols)),
                          by = keys, suffix = c("_corrected", "_previous"))
  write_csv(comparison, file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR, paste0(object, "_Previous_vs_Corrected.csv")))
}
compare_old_results(file.path(LEGACY_DATA_DIR,"Phase3_1_Annual_Results.RData"),
                    "results_annual", results_annual, "variable")
compare_old_results(file.path(LEGACY_DATA_DIR,"Phase3_2_Seasonal_Results.RData"),
                    "results_seasonal", results_seasonal, c("season","variable"))

# Compatibility exports use the original object/file names in the NEW folder.
save(results_annual, annual_df,
     file=file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR,"Phase3_1_Annual_Results.RData"))
save(results_seasonal, seasonal_df,
     file=file.path(OUTPUT_DATA_DIR,"Phase3_2_Seasonal_Results.RData"))
```

## 4.2 Trend figures

Lines use the same slope and median intercept as the residual model. Forest
plots separate energy units from exceedance fractions; seasonal forest panels
compare four seasons within each variable. Colours identify nominal PWMK
significance and are independent of the bootstrap intervals. P-values are
included in labels rather than placed beyond the axis where they can be clipped.

```{r annual-trend-series}

  mutate(

                       levels = unname(VAR_LABELS[ALL_VARS]))
  )

annual_long <- annual_df %>%

# ── Figure 3.1: Annual time series ──────────────────────────────────────

    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = SUBTITLE_SIZE, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(file.path(FIG_PHASE3, "Fig3.1_Annual_Trends.png"),
       p_annual, width = 12, height = 14, dpi = 300)
```

```{r trend-forest-figures}
#| eval: !expr MAKE_FIGURES
# Label p-values beside the VARIABLE instead of beyond the CI endpoint.
# This prevents clipping and separates unlike units into their own axes.
annual_forest_panel <- function(d, units) {
  d <- d %>% mutate(row_label = paste0(label,"   (p ",ifelse(p_value<0.001,"< 0.001",paste0("= ",formatC(p_value,digits=3,format="f"))),")"),
                    row_label = factor(row_label,levels=rev(row_label)))
  ggplot(d,aes(x=slope_dec,y=row_label,colour=significant)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0,linetype="dashed",colour="grey55") +
    geom_segment(aes(x=ci_lower,xend=ci_upper,yend=row_label),linewidth=0.9) +
    geom_point(size=3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=c("FALSE"="grey55","TRUE"="#D73027"),
                        name="Nominal PWMK",labels=c("FALSE"=paste("p >=",ALPHA),"TRUE"=paste("p <",ALPHA))) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0.08,0.08))) +
    labs(x=units,y=NULL) + theme_bw(base_size=BASE_SIZE) +
    theme(legend.position="bottom",panel.grid.minor=element_blank())
}
energy_forest <- annual_forest_panel(
  filter(results_annual,variable!="exceed_p95_freq"),"Zhang slope [m² s⁻² per decade]")
frequency_forest <- annual_forest_panel(
  filter(results_annual,variable=="exceed_p95_freq"),"Zhang slope [fraction per decade]")
p_forest <- (energy_forest/frequency_forest) +
  plot_layout(heights=c(4,1.3),guides="collect") +
  plot_annotation(title="Annual trends and 95% residual block-bootstrap intervals",
                  subtitle="1958–2025 | Same Zhang estimator for points and bootstrap replicates",
                  theme=theme(plot.title=element_text(size=TITLE_SIZE,face="bold")))
ggsave(file.path(FIG_PHASE3,"Fig3.2_Annual_Forest.png"),p_forest,width=13,height=10,dpi=300)
print(p_forest)
```
